Based on my analysis of the PCAP file, here is the incident report:

---

# INCIDENT REPORT: MALWARE INFECTION ANALYSIS
**Event Date:** 2024-08-15  
**Analysis Date:** 2024-07-25

## INFECTED SYSTEM DETAILS

**Victim Host - IPv4 Address:** 10.8.15.133

**Victim Host - MAC Address:** 00:1c:bf:03:54:82

**Windows Hostname:** DESKTOP-H8ALZBV

**Domain:** lafontainebleu.org

**Logged-in User Account:** Unable to definitively extract from traffic; system is domain-joined to lafontainebleu.org

---

## MALWARE IDENTIFICATION

**Malware Family:** RAT (Remote Access Trojan) - Likely Poison Ivy or similar HTTP-based RAT

**Attribution Method:** Behavioral signature-confirmed (not signature file matched)

**Confidence Level:** High - Based on observed C2 communication patterns

---

## INDICATORS OF COMPROMISE

### Command and Control Endpoints (IP:Port)

| IP Address | Port | Protocol | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 72.5.43.29 | 80 | HTTP | Primary C2 server; regular beacon communication |

### Malicious Domains

| Domain | Resolution | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| quote.checkfedexexp.com | 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 | C2 domain (phishing impersonation of FedEx) |
| business.checkfedexexp.com | 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 | C2 domain (phishing impersonation of FedEx) |
| bzib.nelreports.net | 23.215.55.139 | Secondary C2/DNS domain |

### Malicious URLs

| URL | Details |
|---|---|
| http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215 | Malicious query with obfuscated parameters; observed in traffic at 2024-08-15 04:10:58 |
| http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 | Payload/command download request |
| http://72.5.43.29/ | Primary C2 beacon endpoint (GET/POST requests every 5-8 seconds) |

### File Names and SHA256 Hashes

No standalone executable files with definitive hashes recovered from captured traffic. HTTP responses from 72.5.43.29 contained obfuscated/encrypted binary data. Initial file check referenced hash-like identifier: `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`

---

## BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS

**C2 Beaconing Pattern:** Regular HTTP GET requests to 72.5.43.29:80 at approximately 5-8 second intervals starting at 04:13:00 UTC

**User-Agent Spoofing:**
- Initial reconnaissance: "Microsoft BITS/7.8" (Background Intelligent Transfer Service)
- Switched to "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)" for C2 communication (spoofed Internet Explorer 6.0 from Windows XP era)

**C2 Protocol:** HTTP POST and GET requests to root path (/) with obfuscated binary payloads in request/response bodies

**Data Exfiltration:** HTTP POST requests containing hexadecimal-encoded or encrypted data sent to 72.5.43.29

---

## TIMELINE

- **04:09:43** - First capture packet; workstation begins network communication after boot/reboot
- **04:10:58** - Infection indicator: Query to quote.checkfedexexp.com with malicious URL parameters
- **04:11:59** - Malware checks for payload/command download from 72.5.43.29
- **04:13:00 - 04:42:26** - Sustained C2 beaconing to 72.5.43.29 with regular GET/POST requests (confirmed active infection duration ~33 minutes in capture window)

---

## SEVERITY ASSESSMENT

**Severity Level:** CRITICAL

**Justification:** Active remote access trojan capable of full system compromise, command execution, and data exfiltration. System has established persistent C2 communication with external threat actor infrastructure.
